ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nail bed

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic fingernail changes with subungual lesions and discharge, accompanied by scalp lesions
salient_findings: Subungual purpuric lesions
Yellowish discharge from the left thumbnail
Friable tumor with purulent discharge under the left thumbnail
Subungual hemorrhages affecting most fingernails
Erythematous, scaly papules with crusts on the scalp
key_facts: 11-month history of changes in most fingernails
Initial presentation of subungual purpuric lesions
Yellowish discharge from the left thumbnail weeks after initial presentation
Partial improvement with antibiotic treatment
Recurrence and worsening of the lesion
Friable tumor with purulent discharge under the left thumbnail
Subungual hemorrhages affecting most fingernails
Scalp lesions previously diagnosed as seborrheic dermatitis
Biopsies from the nail bed lesion and scalp papules showed a diffuse infiltrate in the upper dermis
Medium-to-large mononuclear cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and reniform nuclei
Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated positivity for CD1a and S100 protein
Negativity for CD68
Testing for the BRAF V600E mutation was negative

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nail bed

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated positivity for CD1a and S100 protein, consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis

shortlist.label: Subungual melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subungual purpuric lesions and hemorrhages could be indicative of melanoma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nail bed
shortlist.why_kept: Friable tumor with purulent discharge under the left thumbnail could be suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Deep fungal infection
shortlist.why_kept: Yellowish discharge and partial improvement with antibiotic treatment could indicate a fungal infection

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse infiltrate in the upper dermis with medium-to-large mononuclear cells could be consistent with sarcoidosis

raw.rationale: The presence of medium-to-large mononuclear cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and reniform nuclei, along with positivity for CD1a and S100 protein, is characteristic of Langerhans cell histiocytosis. The clinical presentation of subungual lesions, friable tumor, and purulent discharge also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Subungual melanoma
rejected.why: The absence of mention of melanin pigmentation or atypical melanocytes in the biopsy results makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nail bed
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not describe features typical of squamous cell carcinoma, such as atypical squamous cells or keratin pearls.

rejected.label: Deep fungal infection
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy results do not support a fungal infection, and the partial improvement with antibiotic treatment suggests a non-fungal cause.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not describe non-caseating granulomas, which are characteristic of sarcoidosis, and the clinical presentation is not typical of sarcoidosis.
